chunks: Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

The sick person prays sitting. If he is unable, he prays lying down. He says Takbir, then recites. When he intends to bow (Ruku'), he closes his eyes, then glorifies (says SubhanAllah), then opens his eyes, so that opening his eyes is raising his head from Ruku'. When he intends to prostrate (Sujood), he closes his eyes, then glorifies. When he has glorified, he opens his eyes, so that opening his eyes is raising his head from prostration. Then he performs Tashahhud and finishes.
ai.seo_question: How should a sick person perform the movements of bowing and prostration while lying down?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific ritual procedure for a sick person performing Salat when unable to stand or bow fully, emphasizing the principle of ease (yusr) in worship. It uniquely prescribes using the closing and opening of the eyes as markers for transitions between Ruku' and Sujood while remaining in a lying position, ensuring the prayer's validity according to Shia jurisprudence. This method highlights the flexibility in physical postures (rukun) while maintaining the essential spiritual intent (niyyah) and recitation.
